results.title: Take one step at a time to achieve sustainability goals - Food Business News
results.content: “You begin with taking every little step and then you start to see it accumulating, so that’s why I equate it to personal finance,” said Chris Wolfe, senior director, environmental and sustainability, Bimbo Bakeries USA, Horsham, Pa. More recently, Bimbo Bakeries USA received the American Baking Association’s Champions for a Better Tomorrow Award for its “Baked for Nature” program, which focuses on carbon reductions and sustainability efforts that Wolfe described as being a part of the company’s broader Nourishing a Better World campaign. Wolfe noted the company is listed as the 40th greenest company in the United States based on electrical energy and has achieved 100% renewable electricity in all bakeries and other buildings.

results.title: Bimbo Bakeries moves to Dallas - Food Business News
results.content: Home » Bimbo Bakeries moves to Dallas. # Bimbo Bakeries moves to Dallas. DALLAS — Bimbo Bakeries USA (BBU), a subsidiary of Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV, has relocated its corporate headquarters to Dallas from Horsham, Pa. BBU said the move “supports greater alignment across US operations and positions the company for long‑term growth.”. In addition to putting corporate leadership closer to key parts of its business, BBU said the Dallas location offers a central position within the United States and puts BBU closer to parent company BBU’s global corporate office in Mexico City. “Relocating our headquarters to Dallas positions us to operate more efficiently as we continue to invest in our brands and our communities.”. While the corporate headquarters is moving, the company’s presence in the greater Philadelphia region will continue through the Conshohocken Sales Center and regional operations, BBU said. BBU shifted its headquarters from Fort Worth, Texas, to Horsham following Grupo Bimbo’s acquisition of Weston Foods in 2009. ## Bimbo Bakeries to close Wisconsin baking plant. ## Bimbo Bakeries to close Nebraska baking plant.

results.title: D-Wave Quantum shares soar 20% as company releases latest computing system - CNBC
results.content: # D-Wave Quantum shares soar 26% as company releases latest computing system D-Wave Quantum's latest quantum computing system has hit the market, the company said Tuesday. "It's an engineering marvel, with substantial technical advancements that highlight D-Wave's progress in scaling quantum technology to meet industry demands for growing computational processing power while maintaining energy efficiency," said CEO Alan Baratz in a press release. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in January said that 15 years was on the "early side" for "very useful" quantum computers, sending quantum stocks spiraling. Baratz told CNBC shortly after the initial comments that Huang was "dead wrong" about quantum computing. Other quantum computing stocks edged higher on the news, including Quantum Computing, Rigetti Computing and IonQ. CNBC logo
